positive.prompt: The billing sync stopped working overnight and the token file says it has an hour left
Our GitHub integration returns 401 every morning and works again after a manual re-login
Verify every third-party credential in this repo is actually usable before we cut the release
The OAuth refresh call returns invalid_grant and I need to know whether a refresh token even exists
Write a health check that proves our connectors still work instead of just checking the config file

negative.prompt: Design the REST contract for the invoice export endpoint
Add structured logging and a trace span around the sync worker
Harden this file upload handler against path traversal

evals.prompt: Our nightly integration health check reports all connectors healthy, but three sync jobs have been failing for a week. Find out which credentials actually work, fix the health check so it cannot report green again, and show the evidence.
evals.expected_output: A per-credential verdict separating missing, expired, and unauthorized, with each credential's type checked against what the client sends, and a health check that fails on authorization rather than on file age.
expectations: Credential types are discriminated by structure before values are compared, so the JWT field holding an opaque string is identified as a type mismatch rather than an expiry problem
Each credential is judged by an authenticated call that requires its own scope, not by the recorded expiry field or the age of the file
The health check reports missing, expired, unauthorized, and ok as distinct outcomes instead of a single healthy state
The authenticated identity is reported for each credential rather than only a pass or fail
The revised check is proven against the fixture's three failure cases and fails on each of them
